Directed reading programs
I have enjoyed participating as a mentor in Dartmouth’s Directed Reading Program for undergraduates. Past reading programs I have supervised include:

Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra, Spring 2025, with Michael Bond.
Markov Chain Monte Carlo and Bayesian Computation, Spring 2024, with Michael Bond and Vadin Thadhani.
Computational Measure Transport, Winter 2024, with William O’Brien and Paul Chirkov.
Markov Chain Monte Carlo and Bayesian Computation, Spring 2023, with Daniel Carstensen.
Bayesian Modeling and Computation, Spring 2022, with Ivy Yan.
Nonlinear Dynamics, Chaos, and Ergodicity, Fall 2021, with Andrew White.

If you are interested in participating in a directed reading program, formally or informally, feel free to email me.

title: Software
text:
Skip to main content





pytikhonov: Tikhonov regularization with GSVD diagnostics and parameter-selection methods.
easygsvd: A Python interface to the generalized singular value decomposition.
blockcg: Pure-Python implementations of block conjugate gradient methods.
gpcg: Conjugate-gradient optimization for bound-constrained quadratic programs.
rjpo: Reversible-jump perturbation optimization for high-dimensional Gaussian sampling.
runningstatistics: Online sample statistics for array-valued data streams.
gsvdm2py: A Python wrapper around MATLAB’s generalized singular value decomposition.

Additional projects are available on GitHub.

Skip to main content








I am a visiting assistant professor of mathematics at The Ohio State University, where I am mentored by Dongbin Xiu. I received my Ph.D. in mathematics from Dartmouth College in 2026, where I was advised by Anne Gelb. My dissertation is titled Advances in Computational Methods for Sparsity-Promoting Linear Inverse Problems. My research interests include (Bayesian) inverse problems, numerical linear algebra, SciML/scientific computing, and uncertainty quantification.
